headline: Probabilistic models now infer haplotypes, local ancestry, and cell and tissue lineages
label: Computational Genome Inference Methods
summary: Recent preprints and a publication apply quantum-inspired, coordinate-based, and Bayesian inference to genotype, ancestry, and lineage data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is joint probabilistic inference of latent genomic or lineage structure from noisy observations. LAML-Pro jointly estimates cell genotypes and lineage trees from genome-editing barcodes under a probabilistic observation model, and BEAM jointly infers cell-lineage phylogenies, tissue-migration graphs, and timing in metastatic cancer within a Bayesian framework built on BEAST 2. QHap casts haplotype phasing as a Max-Cut problem solved with a GPU-accelerated ballistic simulated bifurcation solver, reporting 4- to 20-fold speedups, while PCLAI performs continuous coordinate-based local ancestry inference along the genome. The thread is not shared uniformly: QHap is motivated by computational acceleration rather than a lineage model. What is new is the pairing of coordinate-based and optimization-based formulations with joint inference across genotype, ancestry, and lineage tasks.
